messages.content: Can you get the weather data for Antwerpen by sending a request to the weather API URL? Use latitude 51.2194 and longitude 4.4025, and I'd like the response in JSON format.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

The user says "weather API URL". We might need to ask for clarification. But we can assume a generic weather API like "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". That API uses lat, lon, and format param? Actually open-meteo uses query parameters like latitude, longitude, hourly, daily, etc. But the user wants JSON format. The API returns JSON by default. We can provide a simple request.

Alternatively, we could use "https://api.weatherapi.com/v1/current.json?key=YOUR_KEY&q=51.2194,4.4025". But that requires an API key. We don't have one. So better to use open-meteo which is free and no key.

Thus we can call "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast" with params: latitude=51.2194, longitude=4.4025, hourly=temperature_2m, maybe also windspeed_10m, precipitation, etc. But the user didn't specify. We can just request basic forecast.

We need to set format param? The open-meteo API doesn't have format param. But we can ignore.

We can call the function with url: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast", params: {lat: 51.2194, lon: 4.4025, format: "json"}? But the function expects lat, lon keys. The param names are lat, lon. But the function will send them as query parameters. So the API will receive "lat" and "lon" which may not be recognized. So we need to use the correct param names. But the function's param names are lat, lon. We cannot change that. So maybe we need to use a different API that accepts lat and lon. For example, "https://api.met.no/weatherapi/locationforecast/2.0/compact?lat=51.2194&lon=4.4025". That API uses lat and lon. That might work. But we need to set Accept header to "application/json". The function's default Accept is "application/json". So fine.

Thus we can call "https://api.met.no/weatherapi/locationforecast/2.0/compact" with params: lat: 51.2194, lon: 4.4025, format: "json". But the API might ignore format. But it's okay.

Alternatively, we can use "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=51.2194&longitude=4.4025&hourly=temperature_2m". But we can't set those param names because the function uses lat and lon. So we need to use an API that accepts lat and lon. The Norwegian Meteorological Institute API uses lat and lon. So let's use that.

Thus we call:

{
  url: "https://api.met.no/weatherapi/locationforecast/2.0/compact",
  params: {
    lat: 51.2194,
    lon: 4.4025,
    format: "json"
